correctness.rationale: Exact RK4 identities for q,g were checked by independent symbolic expansion; D>0 on 0<t<12; weighted nonzero relaxation gamma is positive and uniquely determined. The modal energy map implies exact total conservation and the strict Lyapunov identity. The growing bounded winning-energy subsequence proves gamma_n tends to the minimum g; weighted mean then forces all losers to zero. A quadratic with one sign change in the interval proves a unique two-frequency crossing. The exact-rational and direct-RK4 verification script reports 127 passing finite checks; finite tests are corroboration, not proof. Hypotheses exclude zero-step and large-step parameter regimes.

originality.rationale: The 2019 foundational paper already contains the exact type of relaxation and observes modal amplification/damping; this is not presented as a new phenomenon. The new finite-dimensional, all-time Lyapunov-selection theorem and exact classical-RK4 two-frequency crossover were compared by implication against that original full text (esp. §4.1), full texts of 2020 and 2025 relaxation papers, and the 2026 published radial-projection classification. The earlier numerical examples and general energy conservation do not determine the asymptotic winning modes; the radial-projection result concerns a different map and gives a demonstrably opposite winner at the same stable RK4 step. No exact prior statement covering these new claims found in actual searches. Historical priority is qualified and not independently certified.
residual_risks: The original 2019 paper already observes the same RRK4 modal amplification/damping; only its sharpened exact all-time law and crossover are claimed as newly distinguished.
Additional equivalent results in unindexed or differently termed earlier papers cannot be ruled out.
One relevant relaxation-free paper was checked at abstract level only, not used for decisive novelty exclusion.
No independent literature-priority assessment has been performed.

value.rationale: Total-norm preservation is widely used as a numerical safeguard for conservative time integration. The new exact multi-mode selection and crossover distinguish false modal dynamics hidden by that safeguard and, at the same stable RK4 base step, show opposite long-time predictions from two standard norm corrections. This makes a mathematically motivated qualitative diagnostic rather than a routine computational constant; it is not a performance, general multirate, or nonlinear accuracy claim.
